This vignette shows the shortest complete `stormbreaker` workflow for its two
supported tasks:

- binary prediction, where the saved prediction is a class-one probability;
- right-censored survival prediction, where the saved prediction contains a
  risk score and, when a horizon is declared, a survival probability.

The data below are synthetic and are used only to demonstrate software
behavior. They do not establish that either model is suitable for a particular
biomedical study.

```{r load-package}
library(stormbreaker)
predictors <- c("gene_a", "gene_b", "gene_c")
```

## The boundary that prevents external-outcome selection

The development and external parts of the workflow are deliberately separate:

1. create a task from development patients;
2. assess a predeclared pipeline on shared outer folds;
3. choose and fit the final pipeline without inspecting external outcomes;
4. predict an external predictor table that contains no outcome columns;
5. create a separate outcome-only endpoint;
6. evaluate the already saved predictions by exact patient ID.

The example code has all synthetic columns in memory, but the call to
`predict_final()` receives only patient IDs and predictors. In a real study,
the same boundary should be enforced by study design and data access, not only
by code.

## Binary prediction

Create one development sample and one untouched demonstration sample.

```{r binary-data}
binary_data <- bi_example(n = 120L, seed = 20260831L)
binary_development <- binary_data[1:80, , drop = FALSE]
binary_external <- binary_data[81:120, , drop = FALSE]

binary_task <- bi_task(
  binary_development,
  id_col = "patient_id",
  outcome_col = "outcome",
  predictors = predictors
)
```

Declare a fixed logistic-regression pipeline and obtain patient-level
out-of-fold predictions. This example has no learned selector or tuned learner,
so it needs no inner resampling.

```{r binary-development}
binary_pipeline <- sb_pipeline(learner = "logistic")
binary_cv <- run_cv(
  binary_task,
  binary_pipeline,
  folds = 3L,
  seed = 101L
)

data.frame(
  status = binary_cv$status,
  complete_oof = binary_cv$complete_oof,
  roc_auc = binary_cv$metrics$roc_auc$estimate,
  brier_score = binary_cv$metrics$brier_score$estimate
)
```

Fit the declared pipeline on all development patients, then predict external
predictors without supplying the outcome.

```{r binary-prediction}
binary_fit <- fit_final(binary_task, binary_pipeline)
binary_prediction <- predict_final(
  binary_fit,
  binary_external[c("patient_id", predictors)],
  id_col = "patient_id"
)

head(
  binary_prediction$predictions[c("patient_id", "probability")],
  3L
)
```

Only after prediction do we create the endpoint and evaluate it.

```{r binary-evaluation}
binary_endpoint <- bi_endpoint(
  binary_external[c("patient_id", "outcome")],
  id_col = "patient_id",
  outcome_col = "outcome"
)
binary_evaluation <- eval_external(
  binary_prediction,
  binary_endpoint
)

data.frame(
  status = binary_evaluation$status,
  roc_auc = binary_evaluation$metrics$roc_auc$estimate,
  brier_score = binary_evaluation$metrics$brier_score$estimate
)
```

## Survival prediction

The survival workflow adds a time unit and a prediction horizon. Here the
horizon is five months.

```{r survival-data}
survival_data <- surv_example(n = 120L, seed = 20260831L)
survival_development <- survival_data[1:80, , drop = FALSE]
survival_external <- survival_data[81:120, , drop = FALSE]

survival_task <- surv_task(
  survival_development,
  id_col = "patient_id",
  time_col = "time",
  event_col = "event",
  predictors = predictors,
  time_unit = "month",
  prediction_horizon = 5
)
```

The fixed Cox model is assessed on the same kind of outer-fold boundary used
for binary prediction.

```{r survival-development}
survival_pipeline <- sb_pipeline(learner = "coxph")
survival_cv <- run_cv(
  survival_task,
  survival_pipeline,
  folds = 3L,
  seed = 102L
)

data.frame(
  status = survival_cv$status,
  complete_oof = survival_cv$complete_oof,
  complete_survival_probability_oof =
    survival_cv$complete_survival_probability_oof,
  harrell_c = survival_cv$metrics$harrell_c$estimate,
  ipcw_brier = survival_cv$metrics$ipcw_brier$estimate
)
```

Fit, predict without outcomes, and then attach the separately constructed
endpoint.

```{r survival-prediction}
survival_fit <- fit_final(survival_task, survival_pipeline)
survival_prediction <- predict_final(
  survival_fit,
  survival_external[c("patient_id", predictors)],
  id_col = "patient_id"
)

head(
  survival_prediction$predictions[
    c("patient_id", "risk", "survival_probability")
  ],
  3L
)
```

```{r survival-evaluation}
survival_endpoint <- surv_endpoint(
  survival_external[c("patient_id", "time", "event")],
  id_col = "patient_id",
  time_col = "time",
  event_col = "event",
  time_unit = "month",
  prediction_horizon = 5
)
survival_evaluation <- eval_external(
  survival_prediction,
  survival_endpoint
)

data.frame(
  status = survival_evaluation$status,
  harrell_c = survival_evaluation$metrics$harrell_c$estimate,
  time_auc = survival_evaluation$metrics$time_auc$estimate,
  ipcw_brier = survival_evaluation$metrics$ipcw_brier$estimate
)
```

## Where inner cross-validation belongs

The two examples use fixed learners. If a pipeline instead contains a
supervised selector or a tuned learner, that learning must happen again inside
each outer analysis fold. `stormbreaker` routes those operations through the
analysis-fold adapter rather than learning them once on the full development
outcome.

The outer results remain method-development evidence. They may describe several
predeclared pipelines on shared folds, but the package does not rank them or
declare a winner. Once results are used to revise a pipeline, they are no longer
independent external validation.

## Find methods and optional dependencies

The package core imports only the packages needed for its common task,
resampling, optimization, and survival infrastructure. Most algorithm engines
are optional `Suggests`: they are needed only when the corresponding learner or
selector is requested. Query learner-level rows to see which engines the local
R library can currently provide:

```{r optional-dependencies}
learners <- sb_pipeline_registry(
  level = "learner",
  check_installed = TRUE
)
table(learners$task_type, learners$dependency_status)

registry <- sb_pipeline_registry(level = "route")
examples <- match(
  c("logistic", "survivalsvm_additive_fixed"),
  registry$learner
)
registry[examples, c(
  "task_type", "selector", "learner", "optional_dependency"
)]
```

Learner-level status locates R packages but does not load an engine or fit a
model. Route-level rows combine the dependencies of the learner and selector.
If an optional engine is absent or fails, that route reports the failure and is
not silently replaced by another learner.

The current runtime registry is R-only: it contains no Python-dependent
pipeline.

## What this vignette does not prove

Successful execution does not prove transportability, clinical usefulness, or
superiority of either example model. Those claims require a predeclared study,
appropriate cohorts, uncertainty analysis, calibration assessment, decision
analysis when relevant, and external data that were not used to choose the
model.
